english.title: Fail to co-operate with the provision of a specimen of breath - preliminary test - maritime offence
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) failed, without reasonable excuse, to co -operate with a preliminary test in pursuance of a requirement imposed under section 6 of the Road Traffic Act 1988 as modified by section 83 of the Railway and Transport Safety Act 2003
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 83 and 82 of the Railways and Transport Safety Act 2003.

english.notes: This offence wording is to be used for offences relating to ships. See also the corresponding offence wordings relating to aircraft H5624 and mechanically propelled vehicles H5623.

other.powersofarrest:
Under section 6D(2) a constable may arrest a person without warrant if -
(a) the person fails to co -operate with a preliminary test in pursuance of a requirement imposed under section 6, and
(b) the constable reasonably suspects that the person has alcohol or a drug in his body or is under the influence of a drug

N.B. In (ii) above, failure to give a breath test is, in itself, insufficient grounds to arrest, the officer must also have a belief that the suspect has alcohol in his/her body.
other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
